home-title: Frontend programmer with interest for design
home-text-1: I am studying Multimedia Design and I am passionate about developing user-friendly websites and web applications. Through my studies, I have gained experience in UX, UI, color theory, typography, SEO, and web development. I aim to specialize in the development and design of digital solutions using tools such as Figma.
home-text-2: When I work on a project, I focus on all elements and how they connect. I find it exciting to create a cohesive and well-functioning identity across a website or web application. I think creatively, ask questions along the way, and never settle for the easiest solution.
offer-text: I work with a methodical and structured approach, focusing on maintaining an overview of tasks through tools such as Kanban and work breakdown structures. I am quick to learn and curious by nature, always seeking to expand my knowledge and skills. To me, a project is not just a task – it is also an opportunity for growth and learning.
figma: I have a strong interest in design, and Figma allows me to turn ideas into visual concepts. I enjoy experimenting with layouts and styles, and I see it as a creative way to explore designs before coding them.
react: I am learning React with a focus on building applications from reusable components. I enjoy thinking logically about how things fit together and how structure can make code easier to maintain and expand.
illustrator: My experience in Illustrator is limited, but I want to become proficient in creating icons and logos. I find it exciting to learn more about vector design and I am motivated to improve my skills step by step.
case-text: The project for the Steno Museum had a strong focus on communicating to children and young people as the primary target group. We received a questionnaire prepared by the museum, which served as the foundation for our UX and design work.
case-li1: I learned to think strategically about different user groups.
case-li2: I learned to adapt the level of communication to the target audience.
case-li3: I learned how to integrate code into a physical exhibition.
WBS-text: We were a group of three, and I acted as project lead. I developed our WBS and distributed the tasks.
WBS-li2: I improved my ability to maintain an overview.
color-text: With the topic of endometriosis, we dedicated a lot of time to developing a color palette that made a bodily and potentially taboo subject more approachable for the target audience.
color-li1: Warm, body-related colors create a calming impression.
color-li2: A sharp and cool contrast color captures attention.
resp-text: It was crucial for the client that the project was interactive in order to engage the target group.
resp-li1: We used gamification to support learning.
resp-li2: We applied non-linear storytelling for a more personal experience.
resp-li3: We designed different levels of engagement to appeal to all segments.
steno-did: Within our team, I served as project coordinator, responsible for delegating tasks and maintaining coherence between design and implementation. I acted as the primary programmer, providing technical guidance, reviewing code contributions, and ensuring the delivery of a responsive and high-quality product.
steno-learn: I learned a great deal about effective teamwork and communication, and I strengthened my creative thinking skills when working with client wishes.
dress-did: I was the most technically skilled member of the team, which gave me the main responsibility for programming and assisting teammates with their challenges. I provided feedback and ideas for design, and I implemented the design solutions created by the others.
dress-learn: I gained significant insight into visual identity through the use of colors and imagery. Working with a design-strong team allowed me to engage deeply with their choices and develop a stronger understanding of cohesive design.
